findings.issue_text: [Medium/api] common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java:45 — `int order()` was added as an abstract method to a public SPI, breaking binary compatibility: any existing third-party CryptoProvider implementation compiled against the previous interface has no `order()` method, so the new `Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order)` in `detectProvider` will throw `AbstractMethodError` at startup; it should have been a `default` method.

[Medium/security] common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:56 — the fail-fast on multiple discovered providers was removed, but `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider` and `WildFlyElytronProvider` all return `order() == 200`, so ties are resolved non-deterministically by ServiceLoader/classpath order; a deployment misconfiguring both FIPS and non-FIPS providers previously failed loudly but can now silently boot with the non-FIPS provider with only a debug-level log of ignored providers — a FIPS compliance hazard.

[Medium/bug] authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:60 — `getBouncyCastleProvider()` returns the provider of the JVM default KeyStore type (typically "Sun"), not BouncyCastle, violating the interface contract and misleading consumers like `BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER` or BC-presence/`isBCFipsEnabled` checks; it should return the actual registered BC provider or `null`.

[Medium/test_gap] authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:56 — the test only round-trips through the provider's own two conversions and never checks the result with `Signature.verify` or known vectors, so symmetric bugs present in both directions (e.g. R/S swap or byte-order error in both encoder and decoder) cancel out and the test still passes.

[Low/data] authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:147 (`integerToBytes`) — when a DER integer component is longer than the expected `len` (curve/algorithm-length mismatch), it is silently truncated to the low-order bytes, producing a corrupted JOSE signature with no error; overflow should be rejected rather than truncated.

[Low/bug] authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:103 (`concatenatedRSToASN1DER`) — there is no check that `signature.length == signLength` on the untrusted token-verification path; a short attacker-supplied signature throws an unchecked `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` from `System.arraycopy` instead of the declared `IOException`, and an over-long one silently ignores the extra bytes.

[Low/bug] authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java:73 (`readInteger`) — malformed input with a zero-length INTEGER (`02 00`) makes `new BigInteger(new byte[0])` throw an unchecked `NumberFormatException`; a parser for potentially malformed input should surface this as `IOException` like the other corruption cases.

[Low/test_gap] authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:42 — `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")` is used without pinning a curve, so the exercised code paths (left-padding vs. the truncation branch in `integerToBytes`) depend on the JVM's default curve; on JVMs whose default isn't P-256 the ES256 test silently exercises truncation and can still pass; the key pair should be generated with an explicit curve/size.

[Low/test_gap] common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:56 — the significantly changed `detectProvider` behavior (sort by `order()`, silent selection on ties, ignored-provider logging replacing the previous exception) has no test coverage, despite being the mechanism that now decides which provider (including FIPS vs non-FIPS) is used.

[Low/performance] authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:108 — dead code in `concatenatedRSToASN1DER`: two `ASN1Encoder` instances are created and written to and immediately discarded; only the third encoder's output is used.

[Low/bug] authz/client/pom.xml:70 — `org.hamcrest:hamcrest` is added as a test dependency but nothing in the change uses Hamcrest (the test uses `org.junit.Assert`); JUnit 4 already brings `hamcrest-core` transitively, so this adds duplicate `org.hamcrest` classes to the test classpath for no benefit and should be dropped or accompanied by an exclusion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:56 — the fail-fast on multiple discovered providers was removed, but `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider` and `WildFlyElytronProvider` all return `order() == 200`, so ties are resolved non-deterministically by ServiceLoader/classpath order; a deployment misconfiguring both FIPS and non-FIPS providers previously failed loudly but can now silently boot with the non-FIPS provider with only a debug-level log of ignored providers — a FIPS compliance hazard.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` no longer throws when multiple `CryptoProvider`s are discovered; instead it sorts by `CryptoProvider::order` descending and returns the first, only logging ignored providers at debug level. In this diff, `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider`, and `WildFlyElytronProvider` all implement `order()` returning `200`, so the comparator ties and the chosen provider falls back to ServiceLoader encounter/classpath order. That makes selection effectively non-deterministic across deployments and can silently select a non-FIPS provider when multiple are present, whereas previously it failed fast.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:56 — the test only round-trips through the provider's own two conversions and never checks the result with `Signature.verify` or known vectors, so symmetric bugs present in both directions (e.g. R/S swap or byte-order error in both encoder and decoder) cancel out and the test still passes.

adjudication.rationale: The new test `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` signs data, then only checks that `asn1derToConcatenatedRS` and `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` are inverse with each other by round-tripping and comparing `rsConcat` arrays. It never verifies the produced signature with `Signature.verify` nor checks against known good vectors, so a symmetric mistake in both conversions (e.g., consistently swapping R/S or applying the same offset/byte-order error in both directions) could still make the round-trip assertion pass. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:147 (`integerToBytes`) — when a DER integer component is longer than the expected `len` (curve/algorithm-length mismatch), it is silently truncated to the low-order bytes, producing a corrupted JOSE signature with no error; overflow should be rejected rather than truncated.

adjudication.rationale: In `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` the helper `integerToBytes(BigInteger s, int qLength)` explicitly truncates when `s.toByteArray()` is longer than the expected `qLength` (`if (qLength < bytes.length) { ... copy last qLength bytes ... }`). This will silently discard high-order bytes rather than rejecting an out-of-range/oversized DER INTEGER (beyond a possible single leading 0x00 sign byte), which can yield an incorrect/corrupted JOSE R/S value without raising an error. The finding matches the diff-grounded behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:103 (`concatenatedRSToASN1DER`) — there is no check that `signature.length == signLength` on the untrusted token-verification path; a short attacker-supplied signature throws an unchecked `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` from `System.arraycopy` instead of the declared `IOException`, and an over-long one silently ignores the extra bytes.

adjudication.rationale: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getEcdsaCryptoProvider().concatenatedRSToASN1DER(byte[] signature, int signLength), the code blindly does System.arraycopy(signature, 0, r, 1, len) and System.arraycopy(signature, len, s, 1, len) where len = signLength/2. If signature.length < signLength, System.arraycopy will throw an unchecked ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (method declares throws IOException but does not guard/translate). If signature.length > signLength, only the first signLength bytes are used and the remainder is ignored. The diff shows no length check or error handling for either case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java:73 (`readInteger`) — malformed input with a zero-length INTEGER (`02 00`) makes `new BigInteger(new byte[0])` throw an unchecked `NumberFormatException`; a parser for potentially malformed input should surface this as `IOException` like the other corruption cases.

adjudication.rationale: In ASN1Decoder.readInteger(), the DER INTEGER length is taken from readLength() and then read(length) is called. If the encoded INTEGER has zero length (e.g., bytes `02 00`), read(0) returns an empty array and `new BigInteger(bytes)` will throw an unchecked NumberFormatException for zero-length input. This method only declares `throws IOException` and does not guard/catch this case, unlike other corruption paths that throw IOException, so malformed input can escape as an unexpected runtime exception.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:42 — `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")` is used without pinning a curve, so the exercised code paths (left-padding vs. the truncation branch in `integerToBytes`) depend on the JVM's default curve; on JVMs whose default isn't P-256 the ES256 test silently exercises truncation and can still pass; the key pair should be generated with an explicit curve/size.

adjudication.rationale: The new test `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` constructs its keypair via `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` without initializing an explicit curve/size. That is verifiable in the diff (line ~42 in the new file). Since the test’s conversions use `algorithm.getSignatureLength()` (ES256/384/512) but the key’s curve is whatever the JVM/provider defaults to, the round-trip assertion (`rsConcat` == `rsConcat2`) can pass even if the test is exercising left-padding or truncation paths in `integerToBytes` due to a curve/length mismatch. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test robustness/coverage issue rather than a production correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:56 — the significantly changed `detectProvider` behavior (sort by `order()`, silent selection on ties, ignored-provider logging replacing the previous exception) has no test coverage, despite being the mechanism that now decides which provider (including FIPS vs non-FIPS) is used.

adjudication.rationale: The diff materially changes `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` to (a) sort providers by `CryptoProvider::order` descending and (b) no longer throw when multiple providers are present, instead selecting the first and only debug-logging the rest (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java). This is new non-trivial selection logic that determines which crypto provider is used when multiple are on the classpath (and `order()` was newly added to the SPI and implemented across providers). The added test (`ECDSAAlgorithmTest`) only covers ECDSA signature encoding/decoding in the new `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, not the provider-detection/selection behavior. So the finding about missing test coverage for the changed `detectProvider` behavior is grounded in the diff.
